**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The document satisfies the **preferred** position for MINCOMMIT — there is no minimum purchase commitment on us at all:

- **§ 2.1 (p0013)** is an affirmative disclaimer: "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall."
- **§ 12 (p0051)** has Vendor acknowledge we made no exclusivity, MFC, or minimum-volume commitment.
- **§ 7.1 (p0026)** bars Vendor from imposing any minimum-use or similar charge not identified in the Order Form.
- **§ 8.2 (p0035)** gives us a 30-day non-renewal right per Order Form, with a reminder mechanic, so no commitment survives without an exit.

The only "shortfall" language (§ 22, p0095–p0096) is a licence-audit usage true-up, not a take-or-pay obligation, and it is expressly a true-up rather than a penalty — outside this rule's scope.

Two items noted but deliberately **not** flagged here, as they belong to other rules and flagging them under MINCOMMIT would double-count the commercial term:
- **§ 7.7 (p0032)** — 15% of annual Fees per week as "liquidated damages" for late payment is an aggressive late-payment remedy against us, but it is a payment-default charge, not a volume commitment.
- **§ 8.1** three-year MSA term is a framework term only; it carries no committed spend, so it is not multi-year take-or-pay.
